title: Char Siu
subtitle: Cantonese barbecued pork with honey glaze
excerpt: Cantonese char siu: pork belly or shoulder marinated in hoisin, soy, honey, and five spice, then roasted at high heat and repeatedly glazed until the exterior is lacquered, deeply caramelised, and irresistibly fragrant.

recipe.sourceNotes: Char siu (literally 'fork-roasted') is one of the most popular and widely recognised dishes of Cantonese cuisine, essential to dim sum and Cantonese roast meats. The name refers to the historical method of roasting the marinated pork strips on long forks over charcoal. The marinade combines hoisin sauce, soy sauce, honey or maltose, Shaoxing rice wine, five spice, and red fermented tofu for the characteristic reddish colour. Commercial char siu often uses red food colouring; the home version achieves a natural reddish-brown from the caramelised sugars and hoisin. The dish is used as a topping for bowls, in bao buns, or alongside rice. Pork shoulder is the authentic cut; pork belly gives a richer, more indulgent result.

content.text: Marinate overnight for maximum flavour and colour. Glaze the pork with reserved marinade every 10 minutes during roasting; this builds up the characteristic lacquered crust. The pork is ready when it is sticky, deeply caramelised, and slightly charred at the edges.

items.preparation: cut into strips about 5 cm wide and 3 cm thick

content.text: Mix the hoisin, soy, honey, five spice, rice wine, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil in a bowl. Add the pork strips and coat thoroughly. Marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight. Reserve the marinade.

Preheat the oven to 220°C / fan 200°C / gas 7. Place the pork on a rack over a roasting tin filled with a little water. Roast for 10 minutes, then brush generously with reserved marinade. Repeat every 10 minutes for 40 minutes total, until deeply caramelised.
Rest for 5 minutes. Slice and serve over steamed rice with spring onion and a drizzle of the pan juices.
